Histological ﬁndings of affected areas include intense inﬂammatory cell inﬁltrates extending into the crypts, with shortening and
forking of these structures, and associated abscesses. The inﬂammation is transmural; ﬁbrosis and histiocyte proliferation are also
seen. Noncaseating granulomatous submucosal and mucosal lesions, which are a hallmark of this disease, are not found in
a majority of biopsy specimens. Granulomas can also be seen in intestinal infections such as in intestinal tuberculosis and
sarcoidosis.
Even macroscopically normal-appearing tissue may yield histological ﬁndings of inﬂammation compatible with Crohn’s
disease, thus indicating that examination of the entire alimentary canal with surveillance biopsies is required before arriving at
a diagnosis.
Inﬂammatory bowel disease and the terminal ileum
